chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: Dave Duncan joins as arranger and lives in the Fields home
summary: Fields hires the white arranger Dave Duncan, and his mother worries about neighbours when Duncan boards at their house.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: tle ahead of the story, but I must mention this, well, it may not be exactly ahead of it, but I spoke about this Phil Dorsey.

And so Dorsey, that all came about after the Gladewater deal, and then Dave Duncan then, something when I came back, my mind told me, now you're trying to build this band, you need an arranger all the time in there. I called Dave Duncan in Ponca City and asked him to come join the band.
Yeah, Dave Duncan was a white guy.

So Dave came on and was grinning and so my mother--you see, we had a big house in Tulsa then and so I said I would like for Dave to stay in one of the rooms. And she said what? She said son, what do you think the people are going to say? He can go and stay anywhere. I said mama, I'm not making enough money

for him to go stay anywhere like he can. Well, you know it's all right but what about the neighbors with a white guy staying here. So I said to her, mama, you're talking like they talk now, they always say it's all right, but. So she finally said if you think you need him and it will be some help to you and it looks like you got carried away with that music, well go ahead, it's all right.
